summary: This bill modifies how the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) handles export control licenses and related guidance, establishes specific standards for license denials, sets up mandatory technical advisory committees for targeted technology sectors, and requires ongoing reviews of rules concerning advanced computing integrated circuits.

affected_groups.effect: Their targeted regulatory guidance or supplemental license requirement communications will undergo standard interagency processing and face automatic termination within 60 days unless formally published as regulations or in the Federal Register.
affected_groups.group: U.S. and Foreign Persons Receiving 'Is Informed' Letters

affected_groups.effect: They are appointed to 3-year terms on newly required technical advisory committees, subject to non-disclosure agreements, to advise the government on technology supply chains, threats, and export controls.
affected_groups.group: Technical Experts, Industry Specialists, and National Security Personnel

affected_groups.effect: Applications evaluated under a presumption-f-denial standard will be subject to newly published standards and factors established by the Secretary of Commerce.

key_provisions: Requires BIS to administer export authorizations tied to 'is informed' letters or similar guidance through the standard interagency process.
Mandates that 'is informed' letters terminate within 60 days of issuing a related license unless BIS publishes a formal regulation or enters the communication into the Federal Register.
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to publish standards and factors used for a presumption-of-denial standard in the Federal Register and submit them to Congress first.
Expands BIS technical advisory committees by requiring the appointment of committees for eight specified technology and procedural topics.

Mandates that the Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with other departments, regularly review and report on the implementation of a 2025 interim final rule regarding advanced computing integrated circuits.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact economic cost of implementing the new committee and reporting requirements.
The specific operational criteria that will be included in the published presumption-of-denial standards before they are finalized and submitted to Congress.
summary_detail.plain_summary: This bill modifies how the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) handles export control licenses and related guidance, establishes specific standards for license denials, sets up mandatory technical advisory committees for targeted technology sectors, and requires ongoing reviews of rules concerning advanced computing integrated circuits.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters administrative procedures for federal export controls and advanced technology oversight, directly impacting how the Department of Commerce coordinates with other agencies, communicates supplemental requirements to entities, utilizes expert advisory panels, and reviews rules for advanced computing integrated circuits.
